summary.title: Build your own 3D renderer
summary.one_liner: You learn the fundamentals of 3D ray tracing by building a renderer one lesson and project at a time, from casting camera rays to shadows, reflections, and anti-aliasing.
takeaways: Rays are cast from the camera through the image plane to find visible objects.
Intersection tests (such as ray-sphere) solve the visibility problem.
Phong shading and shadow rays add illumination and shadows to rendered spheres.
Recursive ray tracing produces reflections, and distributed ray tracing enables anti-aliasing.
Tagged commits per lesson let you start any project from a partial implementation.
summary.summary: This is the course guide for a two-day 3D graphics workshop by Avik Das at Bradfield School of Computer Science. It is organized as a series of lessons, each teaching one foundational concept and followed by a project where the student implements it in their own renderer. The lesson list covers background, camera rays, vectors, intersection tests, Phong shading, shadows, reflections, and anti-aliasing. The source for several renderer implementations is provided, with one commit per lesson so learners can follow along or start from a tagged partial state.
